paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：關於悠閒與奢華的差別、如何解鎖成長，以及美好人生的多種樣貌
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年7月23日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "Achievements are great. It is satisfying to accomplish something. It feels good to win. And many achievements make the world a better place, too.
paragraphs.zh: 「成就很棒。完成一件事會讓人滿足，獲勝的感覺很好。而且許多成就也讓世界變得更好。

paragraphs.en: But also remember to ask, "What am I really trying to accomplish here?" You may realize the goal is not to write a best-selling book or earn that promotion or get into medical school, but rather to build a life you enjoy. And there are many versions of a life you enjoy.
paragraphs.zh: 但也要記得問自己：『我到底想達成什麼？』你可能會發現，目標並不是寫出暢銷書、獲得升遷，或考進醫學院，而是打造一個你樂在其中的人生。而樂在其中的人生，有很多種版本。

paragraphs.en: It is often the case that if you can release the narrative of "I have to do this" to be happy, then a different (but equally lovely) life is waiting for you."
paragraphs.zh: 通常，如果你能放下『我必須做這件事才會快樂』的敘事，另一種同樣美好的人生，正在等著你。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "Plenty of growth can be found in removing your vices, but the real leaps are unlocked when you stop clinging to your comforts."
paragraphs.zh: 「戒除惡習能帶來不少成長，但真正的躍進，是在你不再緊抓著自己的舒適圈時才會發生。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "Whether you have ten years left or a hundred years left, your life is an incredibly brief moment. We know for sure you won't be here in a century.
paragraphs.zh: 「不論你還剩十年還是一百年，你的人生都只是極其短暫的一瞬。我們可以肯定，一百年後你不會還在這裡。

paragraphs.en: But today? Today you are in the Great Game. And this moment you have right now might as well be the most important moment in the universe. Your time is thin. Go out and live fully now."
paragraphs.zh: 但今天呢？今天，你正身處這場偉大的遊戲之中。而你此刻擁有的這一刻，大可以是宇宙中最重要的一刻。你的時間很單薄，出去，活得淋漓盡致吧。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Inventor and author Lin Yutang on leisure vs. luxury:
paragraphs.zh: 發明家暨作家林語堂談悠閒與奢華：

paragraphs.en: "The enjoyment of leisure is something which decidedly costs less than the enjoyment of luxury. All it requires is an artistic temperament which is bent on seeking a perfectly useless afternoon spent in a perfectly useless manner."
paragraphs.zh: 「享受悠閒所需的花費，遠比享受奢華來得少。它需要的，只是一種藝術家的性情——一心想尋找一個完全無用、以完全無用的方式度過的下午。」
出處：《生活的藝術》（1937年）
二、
小說家保羅．科爾賀談韌性：
「我問自己：失敗是必要的嗎？

paragraphs.en: Well, necessary or not, they happen. When we first begin fighting for a dream, we have no experience and make mistakes. The secret of life, though, is to fall seven times and to get up eight times."
paragraphs.zh: 不論必不必要，它就是會發生。當我們初次為夢想奮鬥時，我們毫無經驗，也會犯錯。然而人生的祕訣在於，跌倒七次，就要爬起來八次。」
出處：《牧羊少年奇幻之旅》
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: Challenge yourself to have one new experience this week. When everything around you is familiar, the days turn stale and slip by unnoticed. A surprising experience breathes life into tired days and makes the mind fresh again.
paragraphs.zh: 這週挑戰自己，去經歷一件新事物。當周遭的一切都太熟悉，日子就會變得平淡，不知不覺地溜走。一個令人驚喜的體驗，能為疲乏的日子注入生命力，讓心智重新變得清新。

paragraphs.en: What is one new experience you can have this week?
paragraphs.zh: 這週你可以嘗試的一件新事物是什麼？

emails.subject: 3-2-1: On protecting your mind, the recipe for frustration, and how to spark better conversation

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：關於保護你的心智、挫折感的配方，以及如何激發更好的對話
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年7月16日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "The recipe for frustration is taking on something that requires a whole person, but only giving it half your time.
paragraphs.zh: 「挫折感的配方，就是接下一件需要你整個人投入的事，卻只給它一半的時間。

paragraphs.en: Look at what you're trying to do. What is required? Some things can only be done well when they are pursued with full effort."
paragraphs.zh: 看看你正在嘗試做的事，它需要什麼？有些事情，只有在你全力以赴去追求時，才能做得好。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "It's hard to learn when you feel defensive.
paragraphs.zh: 「當你處於防衛狀態時，很難學到東西。

paragraphs.en: Relax. You are capable and you can recover from whatever you face.
paragraphs.zh: 放鬆下來。你是有能力的，不管面對什麼，你都能恢復過來。

paragraphs.en: You can accept feedback without taking it personally. What is this moment teaching you?"
paragraphs.zh: 你可以接受回饋，卻不必把它當成針對自己。這一刻正在教會你什麼？」
三、

paragraphs.en: "When you ignore a problem that is small enough to handle, it often grows into a problem too big to manage."
paragraphs.zh: 「當你忽視一個原本小到還能處理的問題，它往往會長成一個大到難以掌控的問題。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Film actress and producer Mary Pickford on protecting your mind:
paragraphs.zh: 電影演員、製片人瑪麗．畢克馥（Mary Pickford）談保護你的心智：

paragraphs.en: "All the water in the world cannot sink a ship unless it gets inside the ship. All the negativity in the world cannot sink a person unless it gets inside the mind."
paragraphs.zh: 「世上所有的水，都無法讓一艘船沉沒，除非水滲進了船身。世上所有的負面情緒，也無法擊垮一個人，除非它滲進了心智裡。」
出處：《何不試試上帝》（1934年）
二、

paragraphs.en: French novelist Gustave Flaubert on happiness:
paragraphs.zh: 法國小說家古斯塔夫．福樓拜談幸福：

paragraphs.en: "The secret of being happy consists of knowing how to enjoy yourself—enjoy being at table, in bed, enjoy standing up, sitting down, enjoy the nearest ray of sunshine, the slightest bit of landscape: in other words, love everything."
paragraphs.zh: 「幸福的秘訣，在於懂得如何享受自己——享受坐在餐桌前、躺在床上，享受站著、坐著，享受最近的一道陽光、哪怕只是一小片風景：換句話說，就是熱愛一切。」

paragraphs.en: Source: His private notebook, Souvenirs, written from 1838–1841.
paragraphs.zh: 出處：他 1838 至 1841 年間所寫的私人筆記《回憶》
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: Psychologist and author Adam Grant shares a question for sparking better conversation...
paragraphs.zh: 心理學家、作家亞當．格蘭特（Adam Grant）分享了一個能激發更好對話的問題……

paragraphs.en: "When you meet someone new, don't ask: What do you do? It limits what people share about themselves to a job description.
paragraphs.zh: 「當你認識一個新朋友時，不要問：「你是做什麼的？」這個問題會把對方能分享的內容，侷限在一個職稱裡。

paragraphs.en: Instead, try: What do you love to do? It ignites curiosity and invites people to express their distinctive interests."
paragraphs.zh: 改問：「你喜歡做什麼？」這個問題會點燃好奇心，邀請對方展現自己獨特的興趣所在。」

emails.subject: 3-2-1: On feeling stuck, chasing your dreams, and the secret to life

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：關於感覺卡住、追逐夢想，以及人生的秘密
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年7月9日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "Chase your dreams. It's unlikely they will play out exactly as you expect, but they know the way. No vision is perfect, but it points in the right direction. Let the energy of your soul lead you."
paragraphs.zh: 「去追逐你的夢想。它們不太可能完全照你預期的方式展開，但它們知道路怎麼走。沒有一個願景是完美的，但它會指向正確的方向。讓你靈魂裡的能量帶領你前進。」
二、
「每個人都想要更好的結果。
技巧，先於結果。
練習，先於技巧。
態度，先於練習。

paragraphs.en: It's the willingness to try (and keep trying) that leads to ability."
paragraphs.zh: 正是那份願意嘗試（並持續嘗試）的心，最終帶來了能力。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "Learn to love the interruptions. Find the fun in the delay, the humor in the challenge, the pleasure in the daily commute.
paragraphs.zh: 「學會愛上那些打斷你的事。在延遲中找到樂趣，在挑戰中找到幽默，在每天的通勤中找到享受。

paragraphs.en: A great deal of life is spent dealing with interruptions and waiting for the conditions to turn. We think, "If I can just get past this, then things will open up." But the interruption is not standing between you and your life. It is your life.
paragraphs.zh: 人生有很大一部分，是在應付各種打斷、等待情況好轉。我們心想：「只要撐過這個，事情就會開始順利。」但那個打斷，其實不是擋在你和你人生之間的東西——它就是你的人生。

paragraphs.en: Yes, I prefer hassle-free days too. But you'll rarely find a situation that is all bad. There are little pockets of joy folded inside the annoyances we face. There is always fun to be had, if you go looking for it.
paragraphs.zh: 沒錯，我也比較喜歡沒有麻煩的日子。但你很少能找到一個完全糟糕透頂的處境。在我們面對的種種煩心事裡，總是藏著一些小小的快樂口袋。只要你願意去找，永遠都有樂趣可以發現。

paragraphs.en: This is one of the arts of living. It's the art of enjoying the imperfect days. It's the art of making all the moments count."
paragraphs.zh: 這是生活的藝術之一：享受不完美日子的藝術，讓每個時刻都算數的藝術。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、
投資人查理．蒙格（Charlie Munger）談努力：

paragraphs.en: "You climb as hard as you can... just advancing one inch at a time. That's the secret of life."
paragraphs.zh: 「你盡全力往上爬……一次只前進一吋。這就是人生的秘密。」

paragraphs.en: Source: Daily Journal Corporation annual shareholder meeting (Feb 15, 2023)
paragraphs.zh: 出處：2023年2月15日每日期刊公司股東年會
二、

paragraphs.en: Poet and novelist Hermann Hesse on the beautiful, fleeting, and precious shortness of life:
paragraphs.zh: 詩人、小說家赫曼．赫塞（Hermann Hesse）談生命之美、稍縱即逝與珍貴的短暫：

paragraphs.en: "This day will never come again and anyone who fails to eat and drink and taste and smell it will never have it offered to them again in all eternity. The sun will never shine as it does today."
paragraphs.zh: 「今天這一天永遠不會再來，任何沒有去品嘗、去嗅聞、去體會這一天的人，直到永遠，都不會再有第二次機會。太陽永遠不會再像今天這樣照耀。」
出處：《克林索的最後夏天》
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: When you find yourself feeling stuck or beginning to dwell on what you can't do, regain control with this simple question:
paragraphs.zh: 當你發現自己感覺卡住了、或是開始糾結在自己「做不到」的事情上時，用這個簡單的問題重新拿回主導權：
我可以做什麼？

emails.subject: 3-2-1: How luck works, why improvement is hard, and a call for courage

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：幸運如何運作、為什麼進步這麼難，以及一聲鼓勵勇氣的呼喚
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年7月2日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "Talent is a gift. Reliability is a choice.
paragraphs.zh: 「天賦是一份禮物。可靠，則是一種選擇。

paragraphs.en: But every family, team, and organization needs reliability just as much as they need talent.”
paragraphs.zh: 但無論是家庭、團隊還是組織，需要「可靠」的程度，其實不亞於需要「天賦」。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "What we call luck is often not purely random, but rather the delayed byproduct of consistently putting yourself in good positions."
paragraphs.zh: 「我們所謂的運氣，通常不是純粹的隨機事件，而是你持續把自己放在好位置上，所延遲出現的副產品。」
三、
「為什麼進步這麼難？

paragraphs.en: Part of the issue is everyone wants to improve, but nobody wants to destroy. Change often requires destruction. Or, at least, unlearning.
paragraphs.zh: 部分原因在於：每個人都想要進步，但沒有人想要「破壞」。改變往往需要破壞，或者至少需要「卸下」原本學會的東西。

paragraphs.en: Let's call it gentle elimination. You may have to leave little habits, update current beliefs, eliminate comfortable patterns. When you want better outcomes, your daily norms may need to change. The process of improvement is not just about adding things you like.
paragraphs.zh: 我們姑且稱它為「溫柔的淘汰」。你可能得放下一些小習慣、更新目前的信念、消除一些舒適的模式。當你想要更好的結果時，你日常的常態可能也得跟著改變。進步的過程，不只是不斷加上你喜歡的東西而已。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes habits and patterns belong to who you were, not who you are trying to be. If you'd like something better, then a routine you are comfortable with may have to die."
paragraphs.zh: 有些習慣與模式，屬於「過去的你」，而不是「你正在努力成為的那個人」。如果你想要更好的東西，那麼你目前習慣、感到舒適的日常，可能就必須「死去」。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Poet Mikko Harvey reminds us that the chapters of life go fast and we don't get much time with the people we love:
paragraphs.zh: 詩人米可．哈維（Mikko Harvey）提醒我們，人生的篇章翻得很快，我們和所愛的人相處的時間並不多：

paragraphs.en: "The number of hours we have together is actually not so large. Please linger near the door uncomfortably instead of just leaving. Please forget your scarf in my life and come back later for it."
paragraphs.zh: 「我們能共處的時數，其實並沒有想像中那麼多。請你在門邊尷尬地多逗留一會兒，而不是就這樣離開。請把你的圍巾忘在我的生命裡，之後再回來拿。」
出處：〈致 M〉
二、

paragraphs.en: A poem from W.H. Auden on courage and commitment:
paragraphs.zh: W. H. 奧登（W.H. Auden）的一首詩，談勇氣與承諾：

paragraphs.en:
"The sense of danger must not disappear:
The way is certainly both short and steep,
However gradual it looks from here;
Look if you like, but you will have to leap."
paragraphs.zh:
「危機感絕不能消失：
這條路確實又短又陡，
儘管從這裡看起來循序漸進；
你可以先看看，但終究得縱身一躍。」
出處：〈先跳，再看〉（1940年12月）
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: Observing greatness can inspire us to be great ourselves. Noticing high-quality work can motivate us to improve our craft.
paragraphs.zh: 看見卓越，能激勵我們自己也變得卓越。留意高品質的作品，能激勵我們精進自己的技藝。

paragraphs.en: What do you keep near you because it is beautiful?
paragraphs.zh: 有什麼東西，是你因為它的美，而一直留在身邊的？

emails.subject: 3-2-1: On the power of trees, celebrating others, and how to have better ideas

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：樹木的力量、為別人喝采，以及如何想出更好的點子
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年6月25日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "Your first attempt might not be very good, but nobody's early work is good. There will always be a gap between where you are and where you want to be. And the bridge between that gap is courage. The courage to look foolish in the beginning. The courage to show up again when your early work is criticized. The courage to look yourself in the mirror and say, "I realize I'm not good enough yet, but the only way to get better is to keep working on it."
paragraphs.zh: 「你的第一次嘗試可能不怎麼樣，但沒有人的早期作品是好的。你現在所在的位置，和你想到達的地方，之間永遠會有一道落差。而跨越這道落差的橋樑，就是勇氣。是一開始看起來很傻的勇氣；是早期作品被批評之後、仍然願意再次現身的勇氣；是能看著鏡子裡的自己說：「我知道自己還不夠好，但唯一能變好的方法，就是繼續努力下去」的勇氣。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "One of the more effective ways to force yourself to have better ideas is to create an artificial constraint.
paragraphs.zh: 「逼自己想出更好點子的其中一個有效方法，就是為自己創造一個人為的限制。

paragraphs.en: For many years, I wrote two articles per week and it would often take me over 20 hours to complete each article. Then I said, "If I only had 2 to 4 hours per week to write my newsletter, what would I do?"
paragraphs.zh: 有很多年，我每週寫兩篇文章，每篇文章往往要花超過 20 個小時才能完成。後來我問自己：「如果我每週只有 2 到 4 小時能寫電子報，我會怎麼做？」

paragraphs.en: That artificial constraint led to the creation of the 3-2-1 newsletter, which has become an incredibly popular format. Sometimes you can improve by cutting your options off."
paragraphs.zh: 那個人為的限制，最後催生出了 3-2-1 電子報，如今它已經變成一種非常受歡迎的格式。有時候，你可以透過砍掉自己的選項來獲得進步。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "You should always be rooting for the people you know. Not only because you may need their support tomorrow, but also because it feels good to celebrate something.
paragraphs.zh: 「你應該永遠為你認識的人加油。不只是因為明天你可能需要他們的支持，也因為為別人慶祝，本身就是一件讓人感覺很好的事。

paragraphs.en: Celebration can rescue your day—even if it is someone else's victory. Envy will ruin your day—even if you're actually winning."
paragraphs.zh: 慶祝，能拯救你的一天——就算那是別人的勝利。嫉妒，會毀掉你的一天——就算你其實是贏家。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Writer and speaker Katrina Mayer offers a reminder:
paragraphs.zh: 作家、演講者卡崔娜．梅爾（Katrina Mayer）給我們的提醒：

paragraphs.en: "Time spent amongst trees is never wasted time."
paragraphs.zh: 「待在樹林裡的時光，從來不是被浪費的時光。」
出處：《芥菜種之道》
二、

paragraphs.en: Minister and philosopher Lawrence Pearsall Jacks on living an aligned life:
paragraphs.zh: 牧師、哲學家勞倫斯．皮爾索．傑克斯（Lawrence Pearsall Jacks）談如何過一致的人生：

paragraphs.en: "A master in the art of living draws no sharp distinction between work and play; labor and leisure; mind and body; education and recreation. He hardly knows which is which. He simply pursues his vision of excellence through whatever he is doing, and leaves others to determine whether he is working or playing. To himself, he always appears to be doing both."
paragraphs.zh: 「一個精通生活藝術的人，不會在工作與玩樂、勞動與休閒、心智與身體、教育與娛樂之間畫出明確的界線。他自己幾乎分不清哪個是哪個。他只是單純地在自己正在做的任何事情裡，追求他心目中卓越的願景，然後把「他到底是在工作還是在玩」這個問題，留給別人去判斷。對他自己而言，他永遠覺得自己同時在做這兩件事。」
出處：《透過休閒的教育》（1932年）
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: If you want a plant to grow, you can fuss over it every day—watering, weeding, moving it toward the sun. Or you can place it in the right soil and let nature do most of the work. A seed planted in the right spot often thrives on its own. Life is much the same. Progress is not only about how hard you work, but also about where you decide to work.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你想讓一株植物長大，你可以每天為它操心——澆水、除草、把它移向陽光。或者，你也可以把它種在對的土壤裡，讓大自然去做大部分的工作。一顆種在對的地方的種子，往往能自己茁壯成長。人生也很類似。進步不只跟你有多努力有關，也跟你選擇在哪裡努力有關。

paragraphs.en: Where is your energy better spent right now: pushing harder or planting yourself in better ground?
paragraphs.zh: 現在，你的精力更該花在哪裡：更用力地推自己一把，還是把自己種進更好的土壤裡？

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：改善這個世界、感覺富足，以及管理你的三個自我
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年6月11日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "You don't need to solve every problem right now, only those that stand in your way."
paragraphs.zh: 「你不需要現在就解決每一個問題，只需要解決那些擋在你路上的問題。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "If you are bummed by the state of the world, go build something."
paragraphs.zh: 「如果這個世界的現狀讓你感到沮喪，那就去建造點什麼吧。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "Be forgiving with your past self. What's done is done. No sense in beating yourself up about it.
paragraphs.zh: 「對過去的自己寬容一點。過去的事已經過去了，沒必要一直責怪自己。

paragraphs.en: Be strict with your present self. Win the moment in front of you right now.
paragraphs.zh: 對現在的自己嚴格一點。贏得眼前這個當下。

paragraphs.en: Be flexible with your future self. There are many paths to success. You don't need life to be a certain way to live well."
paragraphs.zh: 對未來的自己保持彈性。通往成功的路有很多條，你不需要人生變成某個特定的樣子，才能過得好。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Historian and philosopher Will Durant on staying young:
paragraphs.zh: 歷史學家、哲學家威爾．杜蘭（Will Durant）談如何保持年輕：

paragraphs.en: "Childhood may be defined as the age of play; therefore some children are never young, and some adults are never old."
paragraphs.zh: 「童年，或許可以定義為「玩耍的年紀」；所以有些孩子從來不曾年輕過，而有些成年人，也從來不曾老去。」
出處：《落葉》
二、

paragraphs.en: Author and finance writer Morgan Housel on money and lifestyle:
paragraphs.zh: 作家、財經作者摩根．豪塞爾（Morgan Housel）談金錢與生活方式：

paragraphs.en: "If we have the same assets and I can earn an 8% annual returns, and you can earn 12% annual returns, but I need half as much money to be happy while your lifestyle compounds as fast as your assets, I'm better off than you are. I'm getting more benefit from my investments despite lower returns.
paragraphs.zh: 「假設我們擁有一樣的資產，我每年賺 8% 的報酬率，你每年賺 12%，但我只需要一半的錢就能感到快樂，而你的生活方式卻和你的資產一樣快速膨脹——那麼即使報酬率較低，我其實過得比你好。儘管報酬較低，我從投資中得到的效益反而更多。

paragraphs.en: Think about that in the context of how much time and effort goes into achieving 0.1% of annual outperformance in this business – millions of hours of research, tens of billions of dollars of effort – and it's easy to see what's potentially more important or worth chasing.
paragraphs.zh: 想想看，這個產業裡有多少時間與精力，只是為了追求 0.1% 的年化超額報酬——數百萬小時的研究、數百億美元的努力——你就會發現，什麼可能才是真正更重要、更值得追求的事。

paragraphs.en: There are investors who grind 80 hours a week to add 10 basis points to their returns when there are two or three full percentage points of lifestyle bloat in their finances that can be exploited with less effort. Outperformance is amazing when it can be achieved, and some can achieve a lot of it. But the fact that there's so much effort put into one side of the finance equation and so little put into the other is an opportunity for most people, companies, and countries.
paragraphs.zh: 有些投資人一週拼命工作 80 小時，只為了讓報酬率多增加 10 個基點，但他們的財務中卻有兩到三個百分點的「生活方式膨脹」，其實只要花更少力氣就能改善。當超額報酬能夠達成時，那確實很驚人，有些人也的確能做到很多。但事實是：財務這個等式的一邊被投入了這麼多心力，另一邊卻幾乎沒人理會——這對大多數人、公司、國家來說，都是一個機會。

paragraphs.en: This is not about living like a monk, hampered by frugality. It holds true at every level of wealth and spending. The value of all money is relative to expectations... The idea that reducing your needs has the same impact as increasing your income – but the former is more certain and in your control than the latter, so it has a higher expected value – is as true for someone spending $15,000 a year as it is someone spending $15 million per year."
paragraphs.zh: 這並不是在提倡要過著像僧侶一樣、被節儉綁架的生活。這個道理在任何財富與消費的層級都成立。金錢的價值，是相對於你的期望而定的……「降低需求」和「提高收入」帶來的效果是一樣的，但前者比後者更確定、更在你的掌控之中，所以期望值更高——這個道理，對一年花 1 萬 5 千美元的人成立，對一年花 1500 萬美元的人同樣成立。」
出處：《最大的報酬》
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: Is this a problem you need to solve or a tension you need to learn to live with?
paragraphs.zh: 這是一個你需要解決的問題，還是一種你需要學會與之共處的張力？

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "Your response to a challenge defines you more than the challenge itself."
paragraphs.zh: 「你如何回應一項挑戰，比挑戰本身更能定義你是誰。」
二、
「跟自己競爭。

paragraphs.en: When you look outside — your rivals, your industry, your luck — there is always something to blame.
paragraphs.zh: 當你往外看——你的對手、你的產業、你的運氣——永遠都能找到可以怪罪的對象。

paragraphs.en: When you look inside — your process, your effort, your rate of learning — there is always something to improve.
paragraphs.zh: 當你往內看——你的流程、你的努力、你學習的速度——永遠都能找到可以改進的地方。

paragraphs.en: Average looks out. Elite looks in."
paragraphs.zh: 平庸的人往外看，頂尖的人往內看。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "A lovely blend: Always reaching. Already enough."
paragraphs.zh: 「一種美好的融合：始終在追求，卻也早已足夠。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Mike Deegan, head coach of the Denison University baseball team, on what it takes to be successful:
paragraphs.zh: 丹尼森大學（Denison University）棒球隊總教練麥克．迪根（Mike Deegan）談成功所需要的條件：

paragraphs.en: "Show up every day. Work hard. Do it with joy. Care more about others than we do ourselves."
paragraphs.zh: 「每天都出現，努力工作，帶著喜悅去做，並且比起在乎自己，更在乎別人。」
出處：《丹尼森人》（2026年4月22日），意譯
二、

paragraphs.en: Movie critic and writer Roger Ebert on life and happiness:
paragraphs.zh: 影評人、作家羅傑．伊伯特（Roger Ebert）談人生與幸福：

paragraphs.en: "I believe that if, at the end of it all, according to our abilities, we have done something to make others a little happier, and something to make ourselves a little happier, that is about the best we can do...
paragraphs.zh: 「我相信，如果到了最後，我們已經盡自己的能力，做了一些讓別人稍微快樂一點的事，也做了一些讓自己稍微快樂一點的事，那大概就是我們所能做到最好的了……

paragraphs.en: We must try to contribute joy to the world. That is true no matter what our problems, our health, our circumstances. We must try. I didn’t always know this, and am happy I lived long enough to find it out."
paragraphs.zh: 我們必須試著為這個世界貢獻一點喜悅，無論我們有什麼問題、健康狀況如何、處境如何，這都是真理。我們必須去嘗試。我並非一直都明白這個道理，但我很高興自己活得夠久，終於發現了它。」

paragraphs.en: Source: Go Gentle Into That Good Night (May 2, 2009)
paragraphs.zh: 出處：《溫柔地步入那良夜》（2009年5月2日）
【給你的 1 個問題】
你今天贏得這一天了嗎？

James Clear

paragraphs.en:

閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年5月28日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】

paragraphs.en: This week, here are three principles I try to live by:
paragraphs.zh: 這週，分享三個我試著奉行的原則：
一、

paragraphs.en: "I'm adaptable. I don't need the day to go perfectly to make it a good one."
paragraphs.zh: 「我很有彈性。我不需要這一天完美無缺，才能把它變成美好的一天。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "It's not my job to tell myself no. The world will offer plenty of obstacles. I don't need to add to them. My mind is my friend. I am my own biggest believer."
paragraphs.zh: 「對自己說「不」不是我的工作。這個世界已經會提供夠多的阻礙了，我不需要再多加一些。我的心智是我的朋友，我是自己最大的支持者。」
三、

paragraphs.en: "I try to live to a standard, not the circumstances of the day. Some days it is easy. Some days it is hard. But I do it either way because that's who I want to be, not because it is always easy to do."
paragraphs.zh: 「我試著依照一個標準來生活，而不是依照當天的處境。有些日子容易，有些日子難。但無論如何我都會這麼做，因為那才是我想成為的人——不是因為做起來總是很容易。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Roman emperor and philosopher Marcus Aurelius on taking the high road:
paragraphs.zh: 羅馬皇帝、哲學家馬可．奧理略談走高尚的路：

paragraphs.en: "The best revenge is not to be like that."
paragraphs.zh: 「最好的復仇，就是不要變成那樣的人。」
出處：《沉思錄》
二、

paragraphs.en: Scottish mountaineer and writer W. H. Murray on the power of commitment and getting started:
paragraphs.zh: 蘇格蘭登山家、作家 W. H. 莫瑞（W. H. Murray）談承諾與開始行動的力量：

paragraphs.en: "Until one is committed there is hesitancy, the chance to draw back, always ineffectiveness. Concerning all acts of initiative (and creation), there is one elementary truth, the ignorance of which kills countless ideas and splendid plans: that the moment one definitely commits oneself, then Providence moves too. All sorts of things occur to help one that would never otherwise have occurred. A whole stream of events issues from the decision, raising in one's favour all manner of unforeseen incidents and meetings and material assistance, which no man could have dreamt would have come his way.
paragraphs.zh: 「在一個人做出承諾之前，總是猶豫不決，總是有退縮的機會，也總是效果不彰。關於一切主動出擊（與創造）的行為，有一個基本真理，若不明白這個道理，將扼殺無數的點子與美好的計畫：那就是，當一個人真正下定決心的那一刻，天意也會隨之而動。各種原本絕不可能發生的事情，都會出現來幫助你。一整串事件會從那個決定中湧現，帶來各種意想不到的際遇、相遇與物質上的協助，是任何人都做夢也想不到會發生在自己身上的。

paragraphs.en: I have learned a deep respect for one of Goethe's couplets:
paragraphs.zh: 我對歌德的這兩句詩，一直懷抱著深深的敬意：

paragraphs.en:
Whatever you can do, or dream you can, begin it.
Boldness has genius, power, and magic in it."
paragraphs.zh:
無論你能做什麼、或夢想能做什麼，就開始去做吧。
勇氣自有它的天賦、力量與魔法。」
出處：《蘇格蘭喜馬拉雅遠征》
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: Who is the best example you know of living with a good attitude and how can you embody that energy today?
paragraphs.zh: 在你認識的人當中，誰是活出良好態度的最佳典範？今天你要如何把那份能量，體現在自己身上？

emails.subject: 3-2-1: On making mistakes, the paradox of creating, and why habits translate

paragraphs.en:
“The most wisdom per word of any
newsletter on the web.”
paragraphs.zh: 「網路上每個字承載智慧密度最高的電子報。」
3-2-1：關於犯錯、創作的悖論，以及為什麼習慣會延續下去
閱讀完整版
JAMESCLEAR.COM | 2026年5月21日
3-2-1 週四快樂！

paragraphs.en: Here are 3 ideas, 2 quotes, and 1 question to consider this week...
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有 3 個想法、2 句名言，以及 1 個問題，讓你這週細細思考……
【我的 3 個想法】
一、

paragraphs.en: "When you lose a game, the score doesn't transfer to the next contest but your habits certainly will.
paragraphs.zh: 「當你輸掉一場比賽，比分不會延續到下一場，但你的習慣一定會。

paragraphs.en: Circumstances are temporary. Sometimes you're winning, sometimes you're losing. Hot, cold. Lucky, unlucky. But your habits travel with you. This is why you want to execute the same way whether the score is 10-0 or 0-10. Not because the score doesn't matter, but because the score isn't what you're actually building.
paragraphs.zh: 處境是暫時的。有時候你贏，有時候你輸；時而順風，時而逆風；時而幸運，時而不幸。但你的習慣會跟著你走。這就是為什麼，不管比分是 10 比 0 還是 0 比 10，你都想用同樣的方式去執行——不是因為比分不重要，而是因為比分根本不是你真正在建造的東西。

paragraphs.en: It's not about winning or losing any given round. It's about doing things the right way. If you have a chance to practice your craft, you want to do it as well as you can (even if you end up losing that day). Your previous reps can save you or betray you. The habits always translate to the next round."
paragraphs.zh: 重點不在於贏或輸掉某一局，而在於用對的方式去做事。如果你有機會練習自己的技藝，你會想盡力把它做好（就算那天你還是輸了）。你過去的練習，可能會救你，也可能會背叛你。習慣永遠會延續到下一局。」
二、

paragraphs.en: "When you are creating something, you will usually find that once things appear 90 percent done, you are actually about halfway there. But you have to create the first 90 percent in order to see the half that needs to be revised."
paragraphs.zh: 「當你在創作某樣東西時，你通常會發現：當事情看起來完成了 90% 的時候，你其實才走了大約一半的路。但你必須先創造出那前面的 90%，才能看清楚剩下需要修改的那一半是什麼。」
三、

paragraphs.en: I recently found this note to myself:
paragraphs.zh: 我最近翻到自己寫給自己的一張筆記：

paragraphs.en: "No sense in thinking small. Don't water down your vision. A remarkable amount can be accomplished if you are willing to think longer term than most and work hard each day."
paragraphs.zh: 「沒必要把格局想小。不要稀釋你的願景。只要你願意用比大多數人更長遠的眼光去思考，並且每天努力，就能完成非常了不起的事。」
【他人的 2 句名言】
一、

paragraphs.en: Ingvar Kamprad, entrepreneur and founder of IKEA, on making mistakes:
paragraphs.zh: IKEA 創辦人、企業家英瓦爾．坎普拉德（Ingvar Kamprad）談犯錯：

paragraphs.en: "Only while sleeping one makes no mistakes. Making mistakes is the privilege of the active — of those who can correct their mistakes and put them right."
paragraphs.zh: 「唯有在睡覺的時候，人才不會犯錯。犯錯，是行動者的特權——只有在行動的人，才能發現並修正自己的錯誤。」

paragraphs.en: Source: The Testament of a Furniture Dealer (1976).
paragraphs.zh: 出處：《一個家具經銷商的遺言》（1976年）
二、

paragraphs.en: Economist and philosopher Adam Smith on happiness:
paragraphs.zh: 經濟學家、哲學家亞當．史密斯談幸福：

paragraphs.en: "What can be added to the happiness of a person who is in health, out of debt, and has a clear conscience?"
paragraphs.zh: 「一個身體健康、沒有負債、問心無愧的人，還能再往他的幸福添加什麼呢？」

paragraphs.en: Source: The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759)
paragraphs.zh: 出處：《道德情操論》（1759年）
【給你的 1 個問題】

paragraphs.en: If your family inherited only your habits (not your things or your money), which ones would be your richest gifts?
paragraphs.zh: 如果你的家人只能繼承你的習慣（而不是你的財物或金錢），哪些習慣會是你留給他們最豐厚的禮物？
